items.title: Run on Water, Climb Anything
items.body: Waterstride lets you sprint across rivers and lakes, splashing at every step. You can walk freely on rooftops, and one click on the street leaps you off any roof, from any height. Climbs reach a building's wall even from an awkward spot.

items.title: The Deck: Your Own Music
items.body: Press P for the Deck, a music player only you hear. Every track of the soundtrack, shuffle and repeat, a live visualiser, and a look for your faction: a phone, a hex deck or a rune tablet. It steps aside in a fight and comes back after.

items.title: Callouts Go Cinematic
items.body: A Callout now opens with black bars and a big 3, 2, 1, and the bars stay for the whole bout. In a fight, a ring of bars round your pet dances to the music and flashes when a skill pressed now lands on the beat.

items.title: Show Off Your Gear
items.body: Shift + right-click any item to drop it into chat in its rarity colour. Others can hover it to read it, or right-click to try it on. Chat text can be copied, Crew tags got a new look, and Dye and Weave pick the piece you wear.

history.label: 19 Oct 2026 · Characters on the server & Callout music

items.title: Your Characters, Kept Safe
items.body: Your characters now live on the server, not on your PC: sign in on any computer and they are there. Every name is one of a kind across the whole game. If someone took your name first, character select asks you to pick a new one before you play.

items.title: Callouts Have a Beat
items.body: Step into a Callout in town and the fight music kicks in. Press an attack skill right on the beat and that hit lands 6 % harder. Find the rhythm and out-hit your rival.

items.title: Saves You Can Trust
items.body: Every trade, Kiosk sale and Crew founding now saves in one go: if anything goes wrong, nothing is left half-done and nothing is lost. Your progress is kept by the server's own database, backed up regularly.

items.title: A Launcher With an Edge
items.body: The launcher has a new angular comic frame, cleaner panels and a sharper PLAY button. The painting slideshow, this news and the past news are right where they were.

items.title: Walk the Walls
items.body: Zone01's buildings and cliffs are ground now. Run straight up a wall onto the roof, leap from wall to wall, and hold on with Grip (it spends Flux while you cling). Fights follow you up there: strike round corners, chase along a face, and leave ground-bound creatures snapping below.

items.title: Two-Hit Attacks
items.body: Every class has a two-hit attack on Hotbar T, with 18 new two-hit Skill Chips to collect. Redline lands harder on the beat, Stances are shared with your Squad, and Wallstride carries you up and over anything 2.2 m tall.

items.title: Instant Response Online
items.body: On a server your character now moves, jumps and casts the moment you press, instead of waiting for the server to answer. Jumps wind up with a crackle of sparks, vaults flow straight into your run, and your pet does the same tricks on every screen.

items.title: Autopilot Passes & Loadouts
items.body: Autopilot comes as a 3, 14 or 30-day Pass. Save whole gear sets as Loadouts and swap in one click. A step picker sits beside every + for quick counts, the Armorer stocks one of each forge material a week, and your portrait shows the colours you wear.

items.title: Real Servers
items.body: Krytical Nova runs on its own dedicated server. Pick one in the Servers window, or press Enter on the title to join the last one you played on. Your characters and everything they own are saved on the server, and friends outside your house can join too.

items.title: This Launcher
items.body: One small launcher keeps the game up to date. It downloads only the files that changed, checks every file against a signed list so nothing can be slipped in, and repairs a broken install with one click.

items.title: Game Masters
items.body: Each server has up to three Game Masters, marked [GM] in chat and over their heads, with a GM chat channel and a GM console of their own to help players and run events.

items.title: A New Opening
items.body: The game opens with the studio crest and the Krytical Nova logo with a glitch, and the cover painting is now the title screen in every faction's skin.

items.title: The Flask
items.body: A refillable Flux reservoir on your potion bar. Buy one from the Apothecary or find one on Hostiles, and top up your Flux in the middle of a fight.

items.title: Stims in Three Sizes
items.body: Every Stim now comes in Small, Medium and Large, so you choose how much to heal for how much it costs. All three are on the Apothecary's shelf.

items.title: The Recall Tag
items.body: Use a Recall Tag from your Pack or Hotbar, hold still for five seconds, and you are back in town wherever you were. Sold by the Apothecary.

history.label: 10 to 12 Oct 2026 · Style, pets & Crew Halls

items.title: Holoweave
items.body: Wear any look you have unlocked over the gear you have on, shared by every character on your account, and dye each piece in your own colours. Weapons take dye on every part, and Morphweave changes your pet's look.

items.title: Pets That Grow
items.body: Four pets with models of their own follow you and play little tricks. The Tidecaller hatches from an egg and grows at 25, 50, 75 and 100 %, and the Emberwing takes to the air beside you.

items.title: Crew Halls
items.body: Every Crew has a hall of its own: a private three-floor home to fit out with Facades and Finishes, built from solid pieces.

items.title: The Apothecary & Armorer
items.body: The first shops are open. The Apothecary sells Stims and Pet Rations; the Armorer sells Common gear and forge materials and runs the forge. Both buy what you sell, and ask first before taking anything Rare or better.

items.title: Three Factions
items.body: Choose the Hegemony, the Null or the Covenant, shape your character in the creator, and play with a HUD in your faction's own skin. Other factions are fair game; your own only in a duel.

items.title: The Forge
items.body: Temper, Fuse, Tune and Reforge your gear at the forge. Luck tips the odds, and as a piece climbs it lights up with a glow round its edge, up to Epic flame and lightning.

items.title: Creds, Trade & Kiosks
items.body: Earn Creds, keep them safe in your Vault, trade face to face with other players, and set up a Kiosk that keeps selling while you are away.

items.title: Squads, Crews & Duels
items.body: Form a Squad of up to five, keep your friends in Contacts, found a Crew, and settle a score with a duel to the death.

patchNotes.heading: New
lines: Waterstride: from level 60 with Run and Jump at rank 20, click water with Run selected to run out across it. You run to the shore, then over the water by the shortest way, and stand on the water where you stop. Click land to run ashore. It costs a little Flux every second; run out and you are carried back to the nearest shore.
Each footstep on the water makes a small splash, a ripple and a splash sound, and a wake follows you.

The Deck (key P): your own music player. It holds every track of the soundtrack except the fight music, in packs. Play, pause, skip, shuffle, repeat, seek, volume and a list of every track. Only you hear it; the town's music goes quiet for you while it plays.

The Deck looks different for each faction: a phone for the Hegemony, a cracked hex deck for the Null, a carved rune tablet for the Covenant. Opening it makes your character pull it out (the Hegemony take out their phone) for everyone to see.
The Roof drop: up on a roof, click the street below and you run to the edge and leap off, from any height, then carry on to where you clicked.

Item links: Shift + right-click an item (or choose Share in chat) to put it in your message, in its rarity colour. Hover a link to read the item; right-click it to try it on your character, or on a stand-in if it is another faction's gear.
Callouts open like a film: black bars slide in with a big 3, 2, 1, CALLOUT! slams in, and the bars stay until the bout ends, however it ends.

The Beat Ring: in a fight, a small ring of bars round your pet dances to the fight music. It flashes when a skill pressed now is on the beat, bursts in your faction's colour when you hit the beat and greys when you miss it. Settings, Audio can switch it off.
Run wind: streaks and curls of air trail behind you when you run, more of them the higher your Run rank.
Every pet's evolution stage has its own icon.

patchNotes.heading: Movement
lines: Vendor stalls, booths and kiosks can't be climbed: Wallstride leaves them alone, and clicking one tells you so.
Rooftops: click another spot of the roof you are on and you walk there.
Jumping down has no height limit any more; only how high you can jump up depends on your Jump rank.
A drop from a tree reaches up to 25 m away (was 14 m).
No more slipping a step after you stop: you stand exactly where you stopped, on your screen and everyone else's.

patchNotes.heading: Combat
lines: Every attack turns you to face your target: plain strikes, skills, charged skills and area attacks alike.
The Arsenal (Skills window) is cleaner: the skill tree and one box beside it for the skill you pick, with what it does and an Enhance button.
Wallstride and Waterstride each have a tile and a card in the Strides tab with their own icon, what they need and what they cost.

patchNotes.heading: Chat and friends
lines: Chat lines can be highlighted and copied, and pasted into the chat box.
Crew tags no longer show in angle brackets: your Crew shows as a small coloured plate beside your name.
On a laptop, using skills after clicking in the Skills window no longer types the keys into chat.

patchNotes.heading: Gear and looks
lines: Dye and Weave: pick the piece you want to change by clicking it on your character in the Equipment window, instead of choosing a tab.
"Buff" is now "ward" everywhere: the Autobuff is the Autoward, with Autoward Passes, and the wards sit centred in its boxes.

patchNotes.heading: Sound and music
lines: Leaving the title screen sounds better: the sting is quieter and fades as the next screen appears, and the next theme comes in smoothly instead of stacking on top.
A new splash sound for every step on the water.

patchNotes.heading: Game Masters
lines: A GM sees every player on the map, on the minimap and the world map, wherever they are (gm.seeall to switch it off).
GM commands take numbers from their lists: gm.pet.anim 3, gm.travel 2 and others.
gm.autoward and gm.kit autoward hand out the Autoward; a GM teleport always takes a player off a wall first.

patchNotes.heading: Fixes
lines: A climb whose foot was hard to reach did nothing and said nothing; it now walks there and climbs, or tells you why not.
A jump down from a roof was sometimes called back for no reason; it now lands.
The Kitsune's tail trail no longer streaks down the road behind you when you run.
